nodes.label: Correlated Subquery
nodes.rationale: Referencing an outer column is what makes it correlated; logically re-evaluated once per outer row, though optimizers often rewrite it as a join.

nodes.label: Nested Subquery
nodes.rationale: Nested is not the same as correlated; SQL Server allows up to 32 levels, but deep nesting is better replaced with CTEs.

nodes.label: Non-Correlated Subquery
nodes.rationale: Independent of the outer query; runs once and its result is substituted into the outer query.

nodes.label: LAST_VALUE Default Frame Pitfall
nodes.rationale: With ORDER BY, the default frame stops at the current row, so it needs ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING; FIRST_VALUE with DESC is simpler.

nodes.label: SQL Logical Processing Order
nodes.rationale: Window functions are evaluated after WHERE/GROUP BY/HAVING, so they must be wrapped in a CTE or subquery to be filtered.

nodes.label: PARTITION BY (window mini-tables)
nodes.rationale: Applies the window function per group without collapsing rows, unlike GROUP BY; must partition by the group key, not a unique or ranked column.

nodes.label: Index in Partition Order (IX_Sales_Customer_Amount)
nodes.rationale: An index on (GroupKey, Value DESC) removes the sort; keep all OVER clauses on the same PARTITION BY/ORDER BY to avoid a second sort.

nodes.label: SET vs SELECT Variable Assignment
nodes.rationale: SET assigns one variable, errors on multi-row subqueries and sets NULL on no rows; SELECT assigns many, takes the last row, and keeps the old value on no rows.

nodes.label: Pattern A: GROUP BY + HAVING + Correlated Subquery
nodes.norm_label: pattern a: group by + having + correlated subquery
nodes.rationale: Easy to read and good for quick interview answers; subquery runs per group and needs one subquery per extra column.

nodes.label: Pattern B: CTE + Window Functions (ROW_NUMBER = 1)
nodes.rationale: Usually a single pass that scales better on large tables; all columns of the max row are available and tie handling is controllable. Show Pattern A first, then offer B as scalable.

nodes.label: Hierarchy Path Variation (NVARCHAR path)
nodes.rationale: Use NVARCHAR and N' → ' because the arrow is not in most VARCHAR code pages; anchor and recursive member must cast to the same type/length or SQL Server raises a type mismatch.

nodes.label: ID Path + LIKE Subtree Matching (/1/2/4/)
nodes.rationale: IDs with delimiters prevent false prefix matches that name paths would cause (Ann vs Anna); LIKE self-join is slow on large tables and drops orphans.

nodes.label: ESCAPE Clause (literal % or _)

nodes.rationale: JOIN produces one row per matching pair, so DISTINCT is needed to match INTERSECT; it is the only method returning columns from both tables.

nodes.label: INTERSECT
nodes.rationale: Compares result sets and removes duplicates automatically; requires same column count and compatible types; treats NULL as equal to NULL.

nodes.label: Atomic conditional UPDATE + @@ROWCOUNT
nodes.rationale: Check and write in one statement prevents overbooking without long locks; alternatives UPDLOCK/HOLDLOCK or SERIALIZABLE cost more blocking.

nodes.label: Opening and closing talk tracks for live tasks
nodes.norm_label: opening and closing talk tracks for live tasks
nodes.rationale: Silence is the most common reason people fail live coding; restate, clarify, state assumptions, plan, time-check.

nodes.norm_label: execution plan warning signs (table scan, key lookup, sort, hash match, fat arrows)

nodes.label: OPTION (MAXRECURSION n)
nodes.rationale: Safety limit on recursion depth; 0 means unlimited and must be used carefully.

nodes.label: Excluding NULL or Empty Strings (IS NOT NULL AND <> '')
nodes.norm_label: excluding null or empty strings (is not null and <> '')

nodes.label: Unpivot Common Mistakes (duplicate blocks, wrong LineNumber, missing NULL filters)
nodes.norm_label: unpivot common mistakes (duplicate blocks, wrong linenumber, missing null filters)

nodes.label: Covering Index (NONCLUSTERED ... INCLUDE)
nodes.rationale: IX_Orders_CustomerID on Orders(CustomerID, OrderDate) INCLUDE (TotalAmount) eliminates key lookups by including SELECT columns.

nodes.label: Approach 2: CTE + ROW_NUMBER (More Performant)
nodes.rationale: Single pass with window functions (ROW_NUMBER, COUNT OVER, MAX OVER) partitioned by CustomerID, filtering rn = 1 AND TotalCount > 1; presented as more performant than the correlated-subquery approach.

nodes.label: De Morgan's Law (AND vs OR)
nodes.rationale: NOT (A OR B) = (NOT A) AND (NOT B). Golden rule: exclude with OR, include with AND. To exclude NULL or empty values use IS NOT NULL AND col <> '' - using OR wrongly keeps empty strings.

nodes.label: Approach 1: GROUP BY + Correlated Subquery
nodes.rationale: Aggregates per customer with HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 and fetches the date of the max transaction via a TOP(1) correlated subquery ordered by Amount DESC.

nodes.label: Query Optimization Steps
nodes.rationale: Analyze execution plan, clear cache, identify bottlenecks, optimize query, add indexes.

nodes.label: Recursive CTEs (Anchor + Recursive Member)
nodes.rationale: For hierarchical data (employee hierarchy, org charts, bill of materials): anchor selects root rows (ManagerID IS NULL), UNION ALL recursive member joins back to the CTE, tracking Level + 1 and optionally building a Path string.

nodes.label: Performance Killers: Implicit Conversions & Functions on Columns
nodes.norm_label: performance killers: implicit conversions & functions on columns
nodes.rationale: Wrapping a column in CAST or YEAR() prevents index use; compare directly or use a date range (OrderDate >= '2024-01-01' AND < '2025-01-01').

nodes.label: Unpivoting Data with UNION ALL
nodes.rationale: Converts multiple columns into rows by stacking one SELECT per column with a sequential LineNumber; each block filters WHERE ColumnX IS NOT NULL to avoid empty rows.
